1) [Seif 1] "They recite Kaddish." Meaning after Pesukei DeZimrah. Taz, seif katan 1. Agur, siman 98, cites Raavad explaining the reasons for the Kaddishim recited during prayer. The first follows Pesukei DeZimrah, because a section of verses has ended. The second follows completion of the Amidah, which is an independent mitzvah. The third follows Kedushah, which is a davar shebikdushah. The fourth follows a psalm, chapter, aggadah, or Mishnah, as Sotah 49a states that the world endures through Kedushah DeSidra and the response Yehei Shemei Rabbah after aggadah. The fifth follows Ashrei at Minchah, which is itself a mitzvah, for one who says Tehillah LeDavid 3 times each day is assured, etc. The sixth follows Kriat Shema of Maariv, because Maariv is optional and some people leave before the Amidah and would otherwise not hear Kaddish. The seventh follows completion of Maariv. No fewer than 7 Kaddishim are recited daily, corresponding to "Seven times a day I praise You." Shibbolei HaLeket; Beit Yosef; Perishah.

The Kaddish after the Minchah Amidah, before Maariv, was not separately counted because it is included by inference from the Kaddish after the Shacharit Amidah. This also explains the expression "no fewer than 7," even though Kaddish after aggadah is not necessarily recited every day: together with the Kaddish after Minchah there are still 7. Perishah. See Levush.

According to the Arizal, 12 Kaddishim should be recited each day. Six are at Shacharit: before Hodu, before Yotzer, after the Amidah, after Kedushah DeSidra, before Kaveh, and before Aleinu. Although the Arizal writes that the final Kaddish is not counted with the ordinary Kaddishim because all the spiritual worlds have already ascended, he concludes that this Kaddish belongs to Asiyah, the level where death exists, and serves to elevate the souls and nefashot in the secret of resurrection. This is why orphans say it upon the death of a father or mother. Torat Chacham explains that the intention is to elevate Asiyah to Yetzirah at the root of the souls of the dead, and this applies from the lowest Asiyah through the highest levels, since every level is called Asiyah relative to the one above it. It is therefore also obligatory.

Two Kaddishim are recited at Minchah, 1 before and 1 after the Amidah. Four are recited at Maariv: before the Maariv blessings, before the Amidah, after the Amidah, and before Aleinu. This is explained in Shaar HaKavanos, discourse concerning Kaddish, and in the prayer text cited above in siman 48. Some additionally recite after Minchah "For the conductor, with instrumental music," followed by Kaddish and Aleinu, producing 13 Kaddishim corresponding to the 13 Attributes. Fortunate is one who serves his Master with joy and intention.

2) Levush writes that Tiskabel Tzelotehon is recited only after the Amidah. Taz cites this and objects that it is not an absolute rule, for during Selichot before dawn Tiskabel is recited after Selichot, since they too contain many supplications like the Amidah. The reason it is not recited immediately after the Shacharit Amidah is that Kedushah DeSidra follows the prayer and belongs to the same general unit of prayer and praise; therefore Tiskabel is postponed until after Kedushah DeSidra so that it also refers to that section. On a day with Mussaf, a full Kaddish with Tiskabel is recited immediately after Shacharit, and after Mussaf another full Kaddish with Tiskabel is recited for Mussaf, which also relates back to Kedushah DeSidra. Levush.

3) There, "They recite Kaddish." Rambam writes that whenever 10 people engage in Oral Torah, even Midrash or aggadah, they recite Kaddish DeRabbanan. Magen Avraham cites Be'er Sheva as questioning Rambam because in his commentary to the end of Avot he writes that the people customarily recite R' Chananya ben Akashya after the chapters because Kaddish is not said over Mishnah alone but over aggadah, based on Yehei Shemei Rabbah following aggadah. The statements can be reconciled. By strict law Kaddish may be recited after any Oral Torah. The special greatness of Kaddish following aggadah is that aggadah draws a person's heart, Israel rejoices, and when they answer Yehei Shemei Rabbah from the joy of a mitzvah it is especially pleasing before Hashem. Therefore the custom arose to conclude Torah study with R' Chananya ben Akashya, an aggadic teaching concerning Israel's merit, so that the Kaddish falls within the category of Kaddish after aggadah. This is a custom rather than the underlying law. Birkei Yosef; Kesher Gudal.

Accordingly, when R' Chananya ben Akashya is recited after Oral Torah in order to say Kaddish, it should be said with joy of heart and enthusiasm. Particular care should be taken when mentioning the Divine Name in the verse, "Hashem desired, for the sake of his righteousness," to pronounce it with proper intention. Because a person is accustomed constantly to reading verses containing the Divine Name, there is concern that habit may cause him to pronounce the Name without intention. One must therefore be exceedingly careful at all times that no Divine Name passes his lips without proper awareness. See above, siman 5, letter 5.

4) One should not recite Kaddish indiscriminately, but only in the established places in prayer or after reading some Torah matter, explanation, exposition of a verse, or similar Torah study. Kaddish should not be recited merely after private supplications composed by Rav Saadia Gaon or other petitions for mercy. Rambam, Responsa Pe'er HaDor, siman 130.

5) The general rule is that Kaddish requires a minyan of 10 adult Jewish males in the same halachic place. Matters of sanctity are not recited with fewer than 10. Those counted must be present and capable of joining the congregation under the rules explained in this siman. One who is separated by circumstances that prevent halachic joining does not complete the minyan merely by hearing the congregation.

6) Once 10 are present and the shaliach tzibbur begins a davar shebikdushah, the continuation follows the laws stated below regarding members who leave. One should take care not to begin Kaddish until the required 10 are actually present. Where Kaddish follows Torah study, the 10 should have participated in, or at least been present for, the relevant learning in the manner required by the authorities.

7) Those answering Kaddish should listen carefully and answer Amen and Yehei Shemei Rabbah with concentration. The greatness attributed by the Sages to Yehei Shemei Rabbah applies when it is answered with full awareness and proper intention, not as an empty verbal response.

8) The shaliach tzibbur should not rush the wording of Kaddish. Each phrase should be pronounced clearly enough for the congregation to hear and answer in its proper place. The congregation likewise should not begin its response before the chazzan reaches the appropriate point.

9) The several Kaddishim of the prayer service correspond to distinct transitions between sections of prayer. One should therefore not move a Kaddish from its established place merely because it was omitted earlier, when doing so would create an interruption in a section where interruption is prohibited.

10) Kaddish after Torah study is connected to the sanctification produced by Torah learning. Accordingly, where only verses, Mishnah, or another Torah section was recited, the customary aggadic conclusion may be added before Kaddish so that the congregation responds after words that draw the heart and arouse joy in Torah.

11) The full Kaddish containing Tiskabel belongs primarily to the completion of a unit of communal prayer and supplication, whereas half-Kaddish marks transitions between sections. The precise form should therefore follow the established location in the siddur and the rulings of the halachic authorities.

12) According to the kabbalistic arrangement, each Kaddish effects an ascent from 1 spiritual level to the next. This is why its placement is exact and why Kaf HaChayyim repeatedly cautions against reciting an omitted Kaddish later in the middle of Pesukei DeZimrah or another section merely to make it up.

13) The orphan's Kaddish before Aleinu has a special function according to the Arizal. Although all the principal spiritual worlds have already ascended, this Kaddish relates to Asiyah and to the elevation of the souls of the deceased in the secret of resurrection. This is the root of the custom for mourners to recite it.

14) The merit of Kaddish is not restricted to the mourner's own parent. The communal sanctification of Hashem's Name is itself the operative matter, while the mourner's recitation is directed toward elevation of the deceased. The person reciting it should therefore say it with reverence, concentration, and concern for the congregation's responses.

15) A person should not create unnecessary Kaddishim merely to increase their number. The established daily number and locations have reasons in both halacha and kabbalah. Additional Kaddishim should be said only where supported by established custom and a proper Torah or prayer section.

16) The essential rule throughout is that Kaddish is a davar shebikdushah requiring the proper congregation, proper location in the prayer order, and attentive communal response. Its sanctity is magnified when it follows Torah study or communal prayer and when both the chazzan and the congregation recite and answer with proper intention.
